source.title: Weed Identification by Single-Stage and Two-Stage Neural Networks: A Study on the Impact of Image Resizers and Weights Optimization Algorithms
source.authors: M. Saleem; Kesini Krishnan Velayudhan; J. Potgieter; Khalid Mahmood Arif

record.tranche_reason: Tests batch normalization in a new setting: a pretrained Faster RCNN ResNet-101 weed detector, measuring convergence and detection mAP.
record.gate_note: The study reports detector mAP and training-loss results, not training classification error. The reported experiments use COCO-pretrained weights, so they do not test random initialization. Cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares training convergence with and without batch normalization in a COCO-pretrained weed detector, testing V6's training-speed component in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report a 1.82-percentage-point mAP improvement and faster convergence with BN, while their best final mAP is 93.44% using RMSProp without BN. Their broader conclusion concerns the complete weed-detection optimization pipeline.
record.recipe_differences: Uses transfer learning from COCO and object detection on a weed dataset; measures detection mAP and convergence rather than training classification error. Tests batch normalization as one component of a broader optimization study.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-normalization epsilon and decay affect reported mAP; BN setting also changes convergence time.

fits_no_version.finding: BN changes final detection mAP: 93.37% with tuned settings, 91.34% with default settings, 76.83% with epsilon 0.0001 and 88.46% with decay 0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final weed-detection performance depends on BN settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding BN improves final mAP by 1.82 percentage points with SGD and 1.05 with Adam, but reduces it by 0.5 with RMSProp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN's effect on final detection mAP depends on the optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Initializer scale and distribution affect convergence and final mAP in the pretrained residual detector; unit standard deviation was unsuitable for convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initializer settings affect optimization in a transfer-learning detector.

record.problems: Transfer learning was used rather than random initialization. The outcome is test-set object-detection mAP, not training classification error. The BN comparisons do not consistently state matched no-BN baselines for each hyperparameter setting; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional BN-specific numeric results bearing on V6 were identified for extraction. Other detector architecture, resizing, initializer, optimizer, and cross-validation results do not measure the batch-normalization claim as specified.

untested.parts: Training classification error from random initialization on CIFAR-10/100, corrupted labels, and size, duration or regularization effects.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the special initialization exceptions.

Activation-matched initialization preserving signals or gradients and enabling faster or deeper plain-network training; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization. Initializer tuning in this pretrained residual detector does not establish those effects.
Stability thresholds, curvature, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Accuracy trajectories at matched training budgets, tolerance of higher learning rates, the named original settings, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Matched pipeline stages report training time of 10 hours without added BN and 8.5 hours with BN at decay 0.99 and epsilon 0.01. Record this separately from the default-epsilon iteration comparison.
missing.locator: Table 4, Effects of initializers and batch normalization

record.verdict_notes: Endpoint mAP sensitivity does not justify limits_scope verdicts on a training-speed claim. Convergence criteria and run-to-run uncertainty are not specified.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network depth and shortcut effects on training error; special initialization of very deep plain networks and normalization-free residual networks.

Whether activation-matched initialization preserves signals and gradients, improves training speed in plain networks, or enables greater depth. The study does compare initializers in a COCO-pretrained detector.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature or sharpness behavior, and loss recovery or divergence.
The named sigmoid/MNIST, VGG/CIFAR-10, and Inception/ImageNet settings; tolerance of higher learning rates; and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: Faster RCNN ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Added batch normalization with decay 0.99 and epsilon 0.01.
rows.locator: Results and Discussion, Batch Normalization; Table 4
rows.note: The authors report an improvement of 1.82% over the preceding weight-initialization stage; this is detection mAP, not classification accuracy.
rows.check: Final test detection mAP increased from 91.55% to 93.37%, but an endpoint mAP comparison does not measure faster accuracy gains or tolerance of higher learning rates.

rows.subject: Faster RCNN ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Added batch normalization; compared convergence steps.
rows.note: The paper attributes faster convergence to batch normalization.
rows.check: The explicit reduction from 50K to 47K iterations is reported for default BN settings: decay 0.99 and epsilon 0.001, not epsilon 0.01. The optimizer section also reports approximately 47K steps for SGD with BN without specifying epsilon.

source_check.correct: The reduction from 50K iterations to 47K steps is reported with default BN decay 0.99 and epsilon 0.001, rather than epsilon 0.01.
source_check.locator_found: Results and Discussion, Batch Normalization, pp. 14–16, lines 1743–1746 and 1791–1793.
source_check.problem: The row assigns the default-setting iteration comparison to the tuned epsilon setting.

rows.subject: Faster RCNN ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Added batch normalization with default decay and epsilon.
rows.note: No mAP for the same setting without BN is stated here.
rows.check: Final mAP does not measure V6's speed or learning-rate claims. The preceding no-BN stage supplies a 91.55% reference; the authors describe 91.34% with default BN as almost equal.

rows.subject: Faster RCNN ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Added batch normalization with smaller epsilon.
rows.note: The paper says this epsilon degraded performance but gives no same-setting no-BN comparison.
rows.check: The 76.83% final mAP measures detection performance under a different epsilon, not training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: Faster RCNN ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Added batch normalization with smaller decay.
rows.note: The paper says smaller decay did not improve mAP; no same-setting no-BN comparison is given.
rows.check: The 88.46% final mAP measures detection performance under a different decay, not training speed or learning-rate tolerance.
